content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket carefully.

The employee: Daniel Gutierrez (E046) requests write access to Payroll.

There are two notes with conflicting information:
- Note 1 (from HR presumably): role Payroll Specialist, employment type full_time, recommendation write. Payroll owned by Payroll Specialist role. Full-time employees can have up to write, admin if role owns system. Requested write is within limits, recommend write.
- Note 2 (from Security): employment type contractor, security training basic, role Payroll Specialist, recommendation read. Security DB shows contractor with basic training. Contractors max out at read without advanced training. Write not permitted. Recommend read.

So there is a conflict: HR says full-time, Security says contractor. The Security note says "security record governs." 

As the Approver, I need to make the final decision. Access policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

If full-time: requested write ≤ write, so grant write.
If contractor with basic training: max read, so grant read (requested write is above max, grant max).

Which record governs? The notes say Security DB shows contractor with basic training, note says full-time but security record governs. Hmm. The team should use the security record as authoritative? The note 2 says "Security DB shows E046 is a contractor... (note says full-time, but security record governs)."

Given the conflicting facts, the approver must decide. The security record typically governs employment type for access purposes, since access is a security matter. So the employee is a contractor with basic training, max read. Therefore grant read.

Let me submit decision: read.

Reason: Security record shows E046 is a contractor with basic security training; contractors without advanced training max at read. Requested write exceeds max, so grant read.
